To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the inverse association of dietary vitamin K intake with the ucOC concentration depends on a function relevant allelic variant in the VKORCI gene.
the inverse association of dietary vitamin K intake with serum undercarboxylation of osteocalcin depends on a functionaly relevant allelic variant in the VKOR C1 gene.

the inverse association between vitamin K intake and the ucOC/iOc ratio depends on VKORC1 +2255 genotype, and that only in carriers with GG genotype did the ucOC/IOc ratio significantly decrease with an increased vitamin K intake.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of factors that modulate the association between dietary intake of vitamin K and serum ucOC, which is a suggested biomarkers of vitamin K status.
the identification of genetic determinants that modulate the relationship between vitamin K intake and vitamin K-dependent proteins in the circulation.
the identification of genetic determinants of the vitamin K status and their influence on the vitamin K–ucOC association.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the inverse association of dietary vitamin K intake with ucOC depends on the genotype of VKORC1.
the inverse association of vitamin K intake and the ucOC/iOc ratio is modulated by VKORC gene variants.
the association between dietary phylloquinones and serum ucOC is modulated by the VKORC 1+2255 polymorphism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effect of vitamin K on the carboxylation of osteocalcin depends on the genetic variant of the VKOK gene.
dietary vitamin K intake is associated with serum ucOC and that this association is modulated by the VKORC 1+2255 polymorphism.
dietary intake of vitamin K is inversely related to serum ucOC in subjects with the VKORC 1+2255 GG genotype.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the association between vitamin K intake and the ucOC/iO ratio is modulated by VKORC gene variants, which may explain the inconsistent associations between vitamin K status and health outcomes in the general population.
the association between vitamin K intake and the biomarker of vitamin-K status ucOC is dependent on the VKORC 1 genotype.
